item.title: A jury in Malta acquits a businessman in the killing of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia
item.description: Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia had written extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles in Malta. She was killed by a car bomb in 2017, at age 53.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
item.description: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

item.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
item.description: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.
item.content:encoded: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.

item.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
item.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

item.title: India's prime minister is wooing the Gen Z while cracking down on them
item.description: Over two months, protesters, most who appeared to be digitally-savvy GenZ, used social media to organize. Government's efforts to respond spotlight how the ruling party appears to be playing catch-up.

item.title: ICE says it now has enough body cameras. And, Congress averts shutdown before midterms
item.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it now has enough body cameras to equip all of its agents. And, Congress votes to fund the government, averting a government shutdown ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Israel bars U.S. citizens over criticism and ties to Palestinian activists, lawyers say
item.description: Travelers from the U.S. and other nations are denied entry to Israel after interrogations about their links to Palestinians, plans to visit the occupied West Bank and opinions of Israel, lawyers say.

item.title: Germany blames Russia for last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
item.description: The German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig airport last month using a drone laden with explosives. It announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among measures.

item.description: Russia's Vladimir Putin is signaling unwavering support for Iran, as Tehran thanks Moscow for backing amid the escalating Middle East war.

item.title: Who is Betancourt, the man behind the company the US is partnering with in Venezuela?
item.description: The man behind the company that the US is partnering with in Venezuela is Alejandro Betancourt. He has faced multiple investigations in Spain, the United States and Switzerland for money laundering.
